item.title: Xi: Ensure stable supply chains
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Xi: Ensure stable supply chains Fair: Business exchanges upgraded President Xi Jinping highlighted on Wednesday China's commitment to working with countries around the world to jointly uphold the multilateral trading system and ensure the stable and unimpeded operation of global industrial and supply chains. Xi made the remarks in a congratulatory letter sent to the 140th edition of the China Import and Export Fair, also known as the Canton Fair, which opened in Guangzhou, Guangdong province, on Wednesday. He commended the significant role of the Canton Fair in promoting trade exchanges between China and other countries since its establishment in 1957, saying that it has become an effective platform for China to expand high-standard opening-up and promote the building of an open world economy. Xi said that under the new circumstances, China is willing to join hands with other countries to expand mutually beneficial international economic and trade cooperation and advance universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, in order to inject fresh momentum into global development and prosperity. Co-hosted by the Ministry of Commerce and the People's Government of Guangdong Province, the fair runs through Nov 4, with more than 30,000 exhibitors and around 340,000 overseas buyers expected to attend. It features products ranging from consumer electronics and new-type energy storage products, to embodied intelligence products and smart medical equipment, with many cutting-edge Chinese-made products making their debuts at the event, according to the Ministry of Commerce. Premier Li Qiang attended the opening ceremony of the fair and delivered a keynote speech. He highlighted that an increasingly open China that is constantly innovating and honors its commitments will bring new opportunities, provide fresh momentum and inject certainty into the world. Noting that market connectivity is not a tool for rivalry, but rather an effective approach to creating incremental growth, Li stressed the country's commitment to promoting the continuous integration and mutual growth of its domestic market and the global market, and to building an open world economy. As a "super seller" and "super buyer", China is also committed to delivering more benefits to its neighbors and creating greater prosperity for all parties, he said. He expressed the nation's willingness to import more high-quality products, especially those with high added value, from other countries, encouraging more countries to lift restrictions and work with China to actively promote the balanced development of trade. While underscoring the importance of promoting mutually beneficial and win-win cooperation, Li said that China is always committed to promoting shared development. Li emphasized that China will continue to promote high-quality development, expand high-standard opening-up, and take active and pragmatic steps to add momentum to the world economy. The actions will include sharing more market opportunities with other countries, expanding more mutually beneficial cooperation and firmly safeguarding the international economic and trade order, he added. While further lowering market access thresholds to welcome more foreign enterprises to invest and thrive in the country, China will strengthen alignment of development strategies with other countries and support Chinese enterprises to invest overseas in an orderly manner, Li said. He also expressed the country's support for the reform and development of the World Trade Organization, and its willingness to work with all parties to explore future-oriented international economic and trade rules and promote universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization. WTO Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala delivered a video address at the opening ceremony, saying that the remarkable development China has achieved offers valuable opportunities for the world. Noting that the Canton Fair is an important platform connecting China with the world, Okonjo-Iweala expressed the hope that all parties will work together to promote WTO reform and build an open, rules-based global trade system. Over the past seven decades, the Canton Fair has grown into China's largest and longest-running international trade fair, with the widest range of products, the largest number of buyers and the highest transaction volume. China's trade in goods rose 17.6 percent year-on-year to 34.78 trillion yuan ($5.2 trillion) in the first eight months of 2026, with exports up 14.6 percent and imports increasing 22 percent, according to statistics from the General Administration of Customs. Earlier on Wednesday, Li attended a symposium in Guangzhou, communicating with representatives of overseas buyers and exhibitors. He noted that in recent years, the enterprises participating in the Canton Fair have engaged in more diversified business exchanges. They are upgrading from mere trade partners to innovation partners that allow for better sharing of the dividends of technological progress, to investment partners that open up more space for incremental market growth, and to supply chain partners that can enhance the ability to prevent risks and withstand shocks, he said. The foreign representatives said that they are willing to cooperate with China for shared innovation and development.

item.title: Flowing with AI's growth highlighted at skills event
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Flowing with AI's growth highlighted at skills event Participants in global competition focus on utilizing new tech, upgrading capabilities Qiu Mengying, 25, is confident that her aircraft engineer job is indispensable and has no fear she will be replaced by intelligent machines. Despite heated debate over the threat to the workforce posed by artificial intelligence, Qiu, a member of an aircraft maintenance training team that participated in the recent 48th WorldSkills Competition, said: "In our profession, AI is just a helper. It is not here to replace us." The seven skills added to this year's event, which concluded in Shanghai on Sept 27, are unique and hard to automate, she added. "These new skills reflect the latest trends in occupational development and industrial upgrading," said Qiu, while demonstrating her aircraft maintenance skills at the China Eastern Airlines exhibition booth. "They send a signal to more students and young people about where career opportunities are headed, while helping them gain a clearer understanding of their own career plans." Future requirements Unlike many standardized and repetitive jobs, the new skills included in the competition offered a glimpse of the expertise workers will need as industries transform and develop. Known as a bellwether of industrial upgrades and employment trends, WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 helped shed light on "irreplaceable occupations" despite AI's spread, said officials and participants. The skills look to tap into the core employment requirements of digitalization, multidisciplinary and specialized skills. They send clear signals that despite the overwhelming application of AI across various cutting-edge sectors — including digital economy, smart infrastructure and modern commerce — humans cannot be replaced by intelligent machines, the officials and participants said. "There are a total of 64 skills at this year's competition, including seven new skills appearing at the event for the first time," Wu Liduo, director general of occupational capacity building at the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, said during a State Council Information Office news conference in Beijing in June.

item.title: Lai masks a separatist agenda
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Lai's 'city upon a hill' dream masks a separatist agenda In his so-called Double-Ten speech on Oct 10, Lai Ching-te, leader of the Taiwan region, portrayed himself as a guardian of peace, a defender of democracy and a promoter of prosperity and spoke at length about building a "city upon a hill". However, the speech was rife with separatist claims and advocacy of "Taiwan independence". Lai continues to resist reunification and distort historical facts relating to World War II in his attempt to challenge the undeniable truth that Taiwan is a part of China. No matter how attractively Lai packages his "Taiwan independence" agenda, he cannot mask its true intent to separate Taiwan from China. And no matter how much he tries to exaggerate the role of external forces, he cannot alter the fundamental reality that Taiwan is a part of China. His so-called "city upon a hill" cannot sustain the separatist illusion. First, Lai's pursuit of separatism under the banner of democracy can't change historical and legal facts. Marking the 30th anniversary of the island's leadership election system, he claimed that Taiwan's future should be decided by the "Taiwan people" as defined by the Democratic Progressive Party. He also repeatedly referred to Taiwan as a "country", attempting to use the island's electoral system as a political basis for his separatist claims. However, elections and political systems cannot be used to alter sovereignty or deny the shared rights and responsibilities of all Chinese people, including Taiwan compatriots, regarding the future of the country. Such attempts are fundamentally flawed and practically harmful. More troubling is Lai's attempt to invoke WWII history and his claim that history should not be "distorted". He linked the issue to the so-called "survival rights" of the "people" on the island as defined by the DPP authorities. It was a clear attempt to reinterpret history and justify separatist arguments. History cannot be rewritten, legal principles cannot be denied, and the fact that both sides of the Taiwan Strait belong to one China cannot be changed. By confusing Taiwan's return to China after World War II with the political confrontation that arose after 1949, Lai is attempting to distort historical facts and undermine national unity. Such political manipulation cannot change the nature of the Taiwan question or challenge the one-China principle. Second, the military expansion will only heighten tensions across the Taiwan Strait. Lai claims that increasing defense spending is aimed at "deterring war" and creating conditions for dialogue based on so-called "equality" and "dignity". However, behind these claims lies a clear push to expand military preparations and pursue "Taiwan independence" through military means. In his speech, Lai proposed transforming Taiwan's strengths in semiconductors, information and communications technology, and precision manufacturing into defense capabilities, while incorporating military industries, security technologies and artificial intelligence into strategic industries. The intention is clearly to deepen the integration of technology industries with military development and bring more economic resources into a system designed for confrontation. Turning technological strengths, which should be used to promote economic growth and improve people's livelihoods, into tools for political and military competition only increases risks for Taiwan's industries. This approach could also involve more enterprises in military cooperation with external forces, disrupting normal cross-Strait industrial and supply chain cooperation. Taiwan's semiconductor and technology industries, developed over decades, should not become political bargaining chips for separatist purposes. Linking these industries with a "Taiwan independence" agenda will neither provide genuine security nor alter the cross-Strait balance. Instead, it will only increase tensions and impose greater economic and security costs on businesses and residents on the island. Third, Lai's reliance on external forces cannot change the reality of the one-China framework. In his speech, Lai claimed that he welcomed dialogue between the Chinese mainland and the United States to manage competition, while at the same time calling for closer cooperation among so-called democratic partners in the "Indo-Pacific" region. These remarks reveal an attempt to leverage external forces to advance separatist goals. Turning to outside powers and provoking confrontation cannot change the historical reality that both sides of the Taiwan Strait belong to one China. Today, 183 countries have established diplomatic relations with China on the basis of the one-China principle. The UN General Assembly Resolution 2758 has made it clear that there is only one China in the world, the Taiwan region is an inalienable part of China's territory, and the Government of the People's Republic of China is the sole legal government representing the whole of China. Seeking "Taiwan independence" with support from external forces and turning the island into a tool in geopolitical competition will only place the security and well-being of Taiwan compatriots at greater risk. "Taiwan independence" pursued through external support has no future, and attempts to achieve it through military means are doomed to fail. No force can stop the historical trend toward national reunification. Persisting on this path will only put Taiwan compatriots at risk and will ultimately be rejected by history. The author is a professor at the Institute of Taiwan Studies, Beijing Union University. The views don't necessarily reflect those of China Daily. item.title: Huamao village turns Long March spirit into rural progress
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Guizhou's Huamao village turns Long March spirit into practices of rural vitalization Huamao village in Zunyi, Guizhou province, was once poor and underdeveloped. Today, it is lush and thriving. In 1935, the Zunyi Meeting helped set the course for the Red Army's Long March. Today, the spirit of the Long March, combined with a practical, hardworking ethos, is helping write a new chapter in the village's rural vitalization. Villagers who have returned to their hometown have opened farmhouse restaurants, while traditional paper-making has been transformed into cultural and creative products. Huamao's annual per capita disposable income has risen from 12,600 yuan ($1,883) a decade ago to more than 29,600 yuan. Last year, the village received 710,000 visits, generating total tourism revenue of more than 24 million yuan. Times change, but the resolve to endure hardship and never give up remains. Click on the video for more.

item.title: China, Togo elevate bilateral ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
China, Togo elevate bilateral ties President Xi Jinping on Tuesday put forward a series of key principles for the constructive participation of all parties in the settlement of hot-spot issues in Africa, stressing that the African people are the true masters of Africa and should play a central role in regional affairs. He made the remarks while meeting in Beijing with Faure Essozimna Gnassingbe, president of the Council of the Togolese Republic, who is on an eight-day official visit to China running through Friday. During the meeting, the two leaders elevated bilateral relations to a China-Togo community with a shared future for the new era. Elaborating on the principles, Xi emphasized upholding fairness and justice, and urged all relevant parties to abide by the purposes and principles of the United Nations Charter and respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the countries concerned. Noting that wars and unilateral sanctions cannot truly resolve differences between countries, he said that it is imperative to uphold mutual respect, conduct extensive consultations, seek common ground while shelving differences, and practice mutual understanding and accommodation. Xi also emphasized the importance of addressing both symptoms and root causes. Efforts should focus on immediate security while planning for long-term development, he said. Gnassingbe said that Togo fully agrees with the principles proposed by Xi, and highly commends China's key role in safeguarding world peace and stability and jointly addressing global challenges. Togo is ready to strengthen multilateral cooperation with China, jointly defend multilateralism and uphold the interests of developing countries, he added. On bilateral relations, Xi called on the two countries to further strengthen exchanges at all levels, deepen the sharing of governance experience and firmly support each other on issues concerning their respective core interests and major concerns. Togo is welcome to make good use of China's zero-tariff treatment and the green lanes for African products exported to China, and further leverage its role as a regional trade and logistics hub, so as to bring more distinctive products from Togo and the region into the Chinese market, he said. Xi expressed appreciation for Togo's efforts to expand cross-border use of the renminbi, saying that China is ready to strengthen bilateral cooperation in fields such as new energy and digital and smart technologies to support Togo's industrialization. Gnassingbe said that during his visit, he witnessed how China's modernization drive has made remarkable achievements and how fine traditional Chinese culture has been carried forward. Such experiences have given him a better understanding of China's governance philosophy and the sources of its success, Gnassingbe said. Noting that the two countries will celebrate the 55th anniversary of diplomatic ties next year, he expressed Togo's willingness to work with China to enhance mutual trust, strengthen dialogue and communication, and intensify enduring and mutually beneficial cooperation. Before visiting Beijing, Gnassingbe made stops in Shaanxi and Fujian provinces. His itinerary also includes Guangdong province.

item.title: Mining cooperation with Africa highlighted at talks
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
Mining cooperation with Africa highlighted at talks President Xi Jinping called on Tuesday for China-Africa mining cooperation to help African countries translate their mineral wealth into development gains to advance the continent's modernization, stressing that those resources belong to Africa and should not become tools of geopolitical rivalry. Xi made the remarks during talks with visiting Botswanan President Duma Gideon Boko at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, where the two leaders announced the elevation of bilateral ties to a comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership. Boko arrived in China on Monday for a six-day state visit, his first since taking office in November 2024. Beijing is the second stop on his itinerary, following a visit to Fujian province in East China with engagements focused on industrial development, technology and investment. The two heads of state witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents covering the implementation of the Global Security Initiative, Belt and Road cooperation, green minerals, health and human resources. During the talks, which followed a welcoming ceremony, Xi called on the two countries to write a new chapter in their friendship, saying that it should be as brilliant and enduring as diamonds, Botswana's leading export commodity. Mining cooperation featured prominently in the talks, with Xi putting forward four proposals for advancing cooperation between China and Africa in the sector. Such cooperation must proceed from the premise that Africa's resources belong to Africa, Xi said. China is willing to share its experience and help African countries formulate mining development plans suited to their national conditions, he added. He called for cooperation grounded in fairness and mutual benefit, saying that China would continue to encourage its companies to improve their operational capabilities, transfer green technologies suited to African conditions and advance South-South cooperation in mining. Xi also urged a stronger focus on high-quality development. China will continue to promote greater value addition in China-Africa mining cooperation and explore innovative financing models that are affordable and sustainable to support Africa's modernization, he said. Calling for a fair and open environment for cooperation, Xi said Africa's resources should not become tools of geopolitical rivalry. China welcomes sincere efforts by all parties to support Africa's development and is ready to work with African countries to create more favorable conditions for business investment and operations, he added. On bilateral relations, Xi recalled that Botswana had voted in support of restoring the People's Republic of China's lawful seat in the United Nations in the 1970s, even before the two countries established diplomatic relations. Today, he said, the two sides are advancing together in pursuit of modernization. China supports Botswana in following a development path suited to its national conditions, Xi said. He urged both sides to further improve their framework for economic and trade cooperation and make full use of the opportunities brought by China's zero-tariff treatment for all African countries with which it has diplomatic relations. China is ready to strengthen cooperation with Botswana in the digital economy, agriculture and animal husbandry, and implement smart education projects to support the country's economic and social development, he added. Boko praised China's development achievements under Xi's leadership, saying that its development experience offers valuable lessons for Botswana. He said that Botswana firmly adheres to the one-China principle and opposes separatist attempts for "Taiwan independence" and any interference in China's internal affairs. Botswana welcomes more Chinese companies to invest in the country, he said, expressing readiness to expand Belt and Road cooperation and strengthen ties in industry, agriculture, mining, innovation and digital transformation to deliver more tangible results. He also welcomed the four global initiatives proposed by Xi, saying that they demonstrate the responsibility of a major country at a time of significant global challenges. Botswana is ready to strengthen coordination with China, uphold multilateralism, promote solidarity among developing countries and advance China-Africa cooperation to make global governance more inclusive and representative, he said. China and Botswana established diplomatic relations in January 1975 and upgraded their ties to a strategic partnership in September 2024. Bilateral trade reached $1.22 billion in 2025, up 21.3 percent year-on-year, according to China's Foreign Ministry.
